option_or_track.text: Departmental Honors Program The Department of Computer Science's honors program consists of an honors track and honors graduation requirements.
Honors Track The department offers a special honors track to qualified students.
Students in the honors track will have their progress reviewed by the honors committee and are expected to earn grades of B or better in their advanced computer science courses (300 level and above).

Students who successfully complete the honors track with a grade-point average (GPA) in their computer sciences courses of at least 3.6 will automatically qualify for graduation with honors in computer science.
Students in the bachelor of science (B.S.) program (honors track) will be prepared to engage in graduate-level work in a doctoral program.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: At most two of the five electives may be taken outside the Department of Computer Science; at least two must be CS at the 300 level or above.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: IMPLEMENTED as group constraints on CS_ELECTIVES (max_outside_subject / min_at_level), not as a program rule.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Students can count no more than three courses that have no prerequisites, or whose prerequisites are only 01:220:102 and 103 (or only 200), toward the seven required electives.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Classifying a course as 'lower-level' needs its prerequisite structure; Phase 6.2 parses prerequisites but the requirement layer does not use them.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Engineering students who take 01:220:200 use it in place of 01:220:102 and 103 and take eight electives instead of seven.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: A school-dependent alternative that also changes the elective count; not representable without a student-attribute condition.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: A maximum of three economics courses taken outside the Department of Economics at Rutgers University-New Brunswick may be applied toward the major.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Course location/transfer provenance is not recorded on StudentCourse.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Which courses make up the 'grade-point average ... in the major'.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Phase 6.4 encodes the 2.0 rule (ECON_MAJOR_GPA) but its scope is not defined by the catalog, so it is reported NOT_EVALUABLE, never computed. Minimum grades and the one-D elective quota are now encoded.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Students who major in economics (220) may not minor in environmental and business economics (373).
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Cross-program restrictions are out of scope.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: At most three (0-3) D courses chosen from a list of linguistics courses at the 300 level or above and/or from the list of approved courses from outside the department.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: The C/D course lists and the approved outside-course list are not published in the catalog.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: An appropriate Rutgers graduate mathematics course may be substituted for the required analysis and/or algebra course, with departmental approval.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Requires departmental approval, which no CoursePilot data records.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Students must notify the mathematics department in writing if they are not following the standard mathematics major option.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: An administrative step, not an academic requirement a record can satisfy.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: At least one of these courses must be at the 200 level, excluding 201, 202, 295, and 296. At least six of these courses must be at the 300 or 400 level, excluding 495 and 496.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Level distribution across the whole major (all eleven courses) is not an engine constraint today.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: A student may petition the department to substitute other courses for those on this list.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Petitions are individual decisions, not data.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: One 4-Credit Content Course and Lab Combination.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: The page does not list which courses form a content-and-lab combination.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: No more than 6 credits of nonclassroom courses such as fieldwork, research, or internships may be applied toward the major.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Course format (classroom vs nonclassroom) is not recorded.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: No more than three 200-level courses (10 credits) may be applied.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: A per-level maximum is not an engine constraint today.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Grade of C or better in 01:830:101 and 01:830:200 to declare.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Admission rule; kept as admission_prose, not degree completion.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Three any-level electives each in a different thematic (see checklist).
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: The thematic checklist is not published in the catalog.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Students majoring in sociology must complete at least six courses (21 credits) at Rutgers University-New Brunswick. Each of the three 300-level core courses must be completed in New Brunswick.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Course location/transfer provenance is not recorded on StudentCourse.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Credit is not given for both 01:640:477 and 01:960:381, nor for both 01:640:481 and 01:960:382.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: A credit-exclusion pair; the choose_n nodes accept either, and the engine uses one course once.
